A tabela de qualidade está na página [Dados](01_dados.qmd#lab-qualidade). ::: ### B.6 Age of CDAs *Terms introduced in this section:* Age band. Definitions are given in the Glossary. #### B.6.1 Age bands **Method.** Distribution of CDAs and stock across age bands. **Data.** ICMS CDA × year panel (1.4), legal entities only, year 2025 [lab: era 2026]; unit of observation: the CDA-year. **How to read.** Grouped vertical bars, one pair per age band (ordered from youngest to oldest); the vertical axis gives the share in percent; the legend distinguishes the share of CDAs from the share of stock. **Interpretation.** A band whose stock bar exceeds its count bar holds debts larger than average. *Output:* Figure `fig_age_bands`; Table `tab_age_bands`. ::: {#cell-c189 .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} AGE_BANDS = [1, 3, 5, 10] AGE_LABELS = ["<=1", "1-3", "3-5", "5-10", ">10"] def band(col: str = "age") -> pl.Expr: return pl.col(col).cut(AGE_BANDS, labels=AGE_LABELS, left_closed=False).alias("age_band") age_bands = collect(panel.filter(pl.col("year") == SNAP_YEAR).with_columns(band()).group_by("age_band").agg( pl.len().alias("n_cda"), (pl.col("stock").sum() / 1e9).alias("stock_bn"))).with_columns( (100 * pl.col("n_cda") / pl.col("n_cda").sum()).alias("pct_cda"), (100 * pl.col("stock_bn") / pl.col("stock_bn").sum()).alias("pct_stock") ).sort(pl.col("age_band").cast(pl.Utf8).replace_strict({l: i for i, l in enumerate(AGE_LABELS)})) fig = go.Figure([go.Bar(x=age_bands["age_band"].cast(pl.Utf8), y=age_bands[c], name=n, marker_color=color(i)) for i, (c, n) in enumerate((("pct_cda", "CDAs"), ("pct_stock", "Stock")))]) fig.update_layout(barmode="group", xaxis_title="Age band (years)", yaxis_title="Share (%)", showlegend=True, legend=dict(orientation="h", y=1.1)) save_fig(fig, "fig_age_bands") save_tab(age_bands, "tab_age_bands") fig ``` ::: {#c189 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: #### B.6.2 Exposure by age **Method.** CDA-years at risk by age, used as denominators for age-specific rates. **Data.** ICMS CDA × year panel (1.4), legal entities only, 2016–2025 [lab: era 2016–2026]; unit of observation: the CDA-year. **How to read.** One row per year of age, with the number of CDA-years and total paid. **Interpretation.** Dividing by exposure ensures that differences across ages reflect behaviour rather than the number of CDAs at each age. *Output:* Table `tab_exposure_age`. ::: {#cell-c191 .cell execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} exposure = collect(panel.with_columns(pl.col("age").floor().cast(pl.Int32).clip(0, 30).alias("age_year")) .group_by("age_year").agg(pl.len().alias("cda_years"), pl.col("paid_flag").sum().alias("cda_years_with_payment"), pl.col("paid").sum().alias("paid"), pl.col("stock").sum().alias("stock")) .with_columns((pl.col("cda_years_with_payment") / pl.col("cda_years")).alias("payment_hazard"), (pl.col("paid") / pl.col("stock")).alias("rate")).sort("age_year")) save_tab(exposure, "tab_exposure_age", fmt="{:,.4f}") exposure ``` ::: {#c191 .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=10} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: #### B.6.3 Age and recovery **Method.** Pearson and Spearman correlations between age and recovery rate and between age and stock. Pearson measures linear association; Spearman is the Pearson correlation of ranks and measures monotone association, robust to outliers. **Data.** ICMS CDA × year panel (1.4), legal entities only, 2016–2025 [lab: era 2016–2026]; unit of observation: the CDA-year. A 20% random sample of CDA-years with positive stock. **How to read.** One row per pair of variables, with both coefficients. **Interpretation.** A large divergence between the coefficients indicates a nonlinear or outlier-driven relation; the formal choice is made in C.2. *Output:* Table `tab_corr_age`. ::: {#cell-c193 .cell execution_count=11} ``` {.python .cell-code} pr = collect(panel.filter(pl.col("stock") > 0).select("age", "rate", "stock")).sample(fraction=0.2, seed=SEED) rows = [] for y in ("rate", "stock"): for m in ("pearson", "spearman"): r, p = corr_pair(pr["age"].to_numpy().astype(float), pr[y].to_numpy().astype(float), m) rows.append({"x": "age", "y": y, "method": m, "r": r, "p_value": p, "n": pr.height}) corr_age = pl.DataFrame(rows) save_tab(corr_age, "tab_corr_age", fmt="{:.4g}") corr_age ``` ::: {#c193 .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=11} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ### B.7 Recovery *Terms introduced in this section:* Enrolment cohort, recoverable stock. Definitions are given in the Glossary. #### B.7.1 Non-accumulated and accumulated recovery Two recovery measures are used throughout. The *non-accumulated* recovery rate of period $t$ is $r_t = P_t / S_t$, the amount paid in $t$ divided by the stock. The *accumulated* recovery of an enrolment cohort $c$ at horizon $h$ is $R_{c,h} = \sum_{k=0}^{h} P_{c,k} / S_{c,0}$, the cumulative amount paid up to $h$ divided by the stock at enrolment. The first describes the yearly performance of the portfolio; the second describes how much of a cohort's debt is eventually recovered. Axis titles state which measure is shown. #### B.7.2 Annual portfolio recovery rate **Method.** Annual non-accumulated recovery rate of the portfolio. **Data.** ICMS CDA × year panel (1.4), legal entities only, 2016–2025 [lab: era 2016–2026]; unit of observation: the CDA-year. **How to read.** The horizontal axis gives the year; the vertical axis the rate in percent on a logarithmic scale; labelled points mark the programme years. **Interpretation.** On a log axis, equal vertical distances correspond to equal proportional changes; the final year covers January to March only. *Output:* Figure `fig_taxa_recuperacao_anual`. ::: {#cell-c197 .cell execution_count=12} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig = go.Figure(go.Scatter(x=annual["year"], y=annual["portfolio_rate"] * 100, mode="lines+markers", line_color=CEMEPI["deep_teal"])) for name, a, _ in PROGRAMMES: y = int(a[:4]) v = annual.filter(pl.col("year") == y)["portfolio_rate"] if v.len(): fig.add_annotation(x=y, y=np.log10(v[0] * 100), text=name, showarrow=True, arrowhead=0, ay=-25) fig.update_yaxes(type="log", title_text="Non-accumulated recovery rate (%, log scale)") save_fig(fig, "fig_taxa_recuperacao_anual") fig ``` ::: {#c197 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: #### B.7.3 Recovery by age **Method.** Annual non-accumulated recovery rate by age band. **Data.** ICMS CDA × year panel (1.4), legal entities only, 2016–2025 [lab: era 2016–2026]; unit of observation: the CDA-year. CDA-years with a valid age. **How to read.** The horizontal axis gives the year; the vertical axis the rate in percent on a logarithmic scale; one line per age band, identified in the legend. **Interpretation.** If recovery declines with age, the lines are ordered from the youngest band at the top to the oldest at the bottom. *Output:* Figure `fig_recovery_age_log`. ::: {#cell-c199 .cell execution_count=13} ``` {.python .cell-code} rec_age = collect(panel.with_columns(band()).group_by("year", "age_band").agg( (100 * pl.col("paid").sum() / pl.col("stock").sum()).alias("rate_pct"))).with_columns(pl.col("age_band").cast(pl.Utf8)) fig = lines(rec_age.filter((pl.col("rate_pct") > 0) & pl.col("age_band").is_not_null()), "year", "rate_pct", "age_band", log_y=True, y_title="Non-accumulated recovery rate (%, log scale)", order=AGE_LABELS, names={l: f"{l} years" for l in AGE_LABELS}) save_fig(fig, "fig_recovery_age_log", width="double") fig ``` ::: {#c199 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: #### B.7.4 Accumulated recovery by cohort **Method.** Accumulated recovery curves by enrolment cohort. **Data.** ICMS CDA × year panel (1.4), legal entities only, 2016–2025 [lab: era 2016–2026]; unit of observation: the CDA-year. Cohorts enrolled from 2016 onward. **How to read.** The horizontal axis gives years since enrolment; the vertical axis the cumulative amount paid as a percentage of the enrolled value, on a logarithmic scale; one line per cohort, identified in the legend. **Interpretation.** Curves that flatten indicate that additional recovery becomes rare after a few years; later cohorts have shorter curves because fewer horizons are observed. *Output:* Figure `fig_recovery_cumulative_log`. ::: {#cell-c201 .cell execution_count=14} ``` {.python .cell-code} def cohort_curves() -> pl.DataFrame: enrolled = attributes.filter(pl.col("DATA_INSCRICAO").dt.year() >= YEARS[0]).select( "ID_DEBITO", pl.col("DATA_INSCRICAO").dt.year().alias("cohort"), "max_value") base = enrolled.group_by("cohort").agg(pl.col("max_value").sum().alias("enrolled_value")) paid = (scan_gare().join(enrolled, on="ID_DEBITO") .with_columns((pl.col("DATA_ARRECADACAO_GARE").dt.year() - pl.col("cohort")).alias("h")) .filter(pl.col("h") >= 0).group_by("cohort", "h").agg(pl.col("VALOR_RECEITA").sum().alias("paid"))) return collect(paid.join(base, on="cohort").sort("cohort", "h").with_columns( (pl.col("paid").cum_sum().over("cohort") / pl.col("enrolled_value")).alias("acc_rec"))) curves = collect(cached("B.7.4", cohort_curves, params=EXTRACT_PARAMS)).with_columns(pl.col("cohort").cast(pl.Utf8)) fig = lines(curves.with_columns(pl.col("acc_rec") * 100), "h", "acc_rec", "cohort", log_y=True, y_title="Accumulated recovery (% of enrolled value, log scale)", x_title="Years since enrolment") save_fig(fig, "fig_recovery_cumulative_log", width="double") fig ``` ::: {#c201 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: #### B.7.5 Distribution of CDA recovery rates **Method.** Descriptive statistics of CDA-level recovery. **Data.** ICMS CDA × year panel (1.4), legal entities only, 2016–2025 [lab: era 2016–2026]; unit of observation: the CDA-year. **How to read.** One row per variable (recovery rate, amount paid, payment indicator) with moments, quantiles and share of zeros. **Interpretation.** A large share of zeros means that recovery is a mixture of non-paying CDAs and a skewed distribution among payers, which motivates modelling the probability of payment separately (D.6.1). *Output:* Table `tab_descriptives`. ::: {#cell-c203 .cell execution_count=15} ``` {.python .cell-code} descriptives = collect(panel.filter(pl.col("stock") > 0).select( *[pl.struct(variable=pl.lit(c), n=pl.col(c).count(), mean=pl.col(c).mean(), median=pl.col(c).median(), sd=pl.col(c).std(), p90=pl.col(c).quantile(0.9), max=pl.col(c).max(), share_zero=(pl.col(c) == 0).mean()).alias(c) for c in ("rate", "paid", "paid_flag", "stock", "age")])).transpose().unnest("column_0") save_tab(descriptives, "tab_descriptives", fmt="{:,.4f}") descriptives ``` ::: {#c203 .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=15} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: #### B.7.6 Recovered over recoverable stock **Method.** Recovery relative to two denominators: total year-end stock and recoverable stock. Recoverable stock keeps only debts in the enrolled administrative situation and excludes those older than ten years that have never recorded a payment. **Data.** ICMS CDA × year panel (1.4), legal entities only, 2016–2025 [lab: era 2016–2026]; unit of observation: the CDA-year. **How to read.** The horizontal axis gives the year; the vertical axis the amount recovered as a percentage of each denominator, on a logarithmic scale; one line per denominator, identified in the legend. **Interpretation.** The ratio to recoverable stock is always the higher one; the vertical distance between the lines reflects the share of stock classified as irrecoverable. The indicator depends on the criterion adopted. *Output:* Figure `fig_recoverable_ratio`. ::: {#cell-c205 .cell execution_count=16} ``` {.python .cell-code} RECOVERABLE_MAX_AGE = 10 def recoverable_ratio() -> pl.DataFrame: ever_paid_ids = scan_gare().select("ID_DEBITO").unique() flagged = panel.join(ever_paid_ids.with_columns(pl.lit(True).alias("has_paid")), on="ID_DEBITO", how="left").with_columns( (~((pl.col("age") > RECOVERABLE_MAX_AGE) & pl.col("has_paid").is_null()) & (pl.col("SITUACAO_DEBITO") == "Inscrito")).alias("recoverable")) return collect(flagged.group_by("year").agg(pl.col("paid").sum(), pl.col("stock").sum().alias("stock"), pl.col("stock").filter(pl.col("recoverable")).sum().alias("recoverable_stock")).sort("year")) rr = collect(cached("B.7.6", recoverable_ratio, params={**EXTRACT_PARAMS, "max_age": RECOVERABLE_MAX_AGE})).with_columns( (100 * pl.col("paid") / pl.col("stock")).alias("recovered_over_stock"), (100 * pl.col("paid") / pl.col("recoverable_stock")).alias("recovered_over_recoverable")) long = rr.unpivot(index="year", on=["recovered_over_stock", "recovered_over_recoverable"], variable_name="measure", value_name="pct") fig = lines(long, "year", "pct", "measure", log_y=True, y_title="Amount recovered (% of denominator, log scale)", names={"recovered_over_stock": "Over total year-end stock", "recovered_over_recoverable": "Over recoverable stock"}) save_fig(fig, "fig_recoverable_ratio", width="double") fig ``` ::: {#c205 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### B.8 Payments over the life of the debt *No new terms are introduced in this section; terms used here are defined in the Glossary.* #### B.8.1 Open and paid CDAs **Method.** Cross-tabulation of payment in the current year and payment since enrolment. **Data.** ICMS CDA × year panel (1.4), legal entities only, year 2025 [lab: era 2026]; unit of observation: the CDA-year. Payment history from GARE. **How to read.** Rows combine the two payment indicators; columns give CDA counts and stock. **Interpretation.** CDAs never paid but still in the stock form the core of non-recovery. *Output:* Table `tab_open_paid`. ::: {#cell-c208 .cell execution_count=17} ``` {.python .cell-code} open_paid = collect(panel.filter(pl.col("year") == SNAP_YEAR).join( scan_gare().select("ID_DEBITO").unique().with_columns(pl.lit(True).alias("ever_paid")), on="ID_DEBITO", how="left") .with_columns(pl.col("ever_paid").fill_null(False)) .group_by(pl.col("paid_flag").cast(pl.Boolean).alias("paid_this_year"), "ever_paid") .agg(pl.len().alias("n_cda"), (pl.col("stock").sum() / 1e9).alias("stock_bn")).sort("paid_this_year", "ever_paid")) save_tab(open_paid, "tab_open_paid", fmt="{:,.2f}") open_paid ``` ::: {#c208 .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=17} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: #### B.8.2 Open and paid CDAs by enrolment year **Method.** Size and payment experience of enrolment cohorts. **Data.** ICMS extract (1.3), CDAs enrolled from 1990 onward; unit of observation: the enrolment year. **How to read.** Bars (left axis) give CDAs enrolled per year in thousands; the line (right axis) gives the percentage with any payment; the legend states which axis each series uses. **Interpretation.** Read the shape of the line rather than its height relative to the bars; recent cohorts have had less time to pay, so their percentage is mechanically lower. *Output:* Figure `fig_open_paid_by_cohort`. ::: {#cell-c210 .cell execution_count=18} ``` {.python .cell-code} by_cohort = cda.filter(pl.col("DATA_INSCRICAO").dt.year() >= 1990).group_by(pl.col("DATA_INSCRICAO").dt.year().alias("cohort")).agg( pl.len().alias("n_cda"), (100 * pl.col("ever_paid").mean()).alias("pct_ever_paid")).sort("cohort") fig = make_subplots(specs=[[{"secondary_y": True}]]) fig.add_trace(go.Bar(x=by_cohort["cohort"], y=by_cohort["n_cda"] / 1e3, marker_color="rgba(21,76,86,0.35)", name="CDAs enrolled (left axis)"), secondary_y=False) fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=by_cohort["cohort"], y=by_cohort["pct_ever_paid"], mode="lines+markers", line_color=CEMEPI["sand"], name="CDAs with any payment, % (right axis)"), secondary_y=True) fig.update_yaxes(title_text="CDAs (thousand)", secondary_y=False, rangemode="tozero") fig.update_yaxes(title_text="With any payment (%)", secondary_y=True, showgrid=False, rangemode="tozero", tickformat=".0f") fig.update_layout(showlegend=True, legend=dict(orientation="h", y=-0.3)) fig.update_xaxes(title_text="Year of enrolment") save_fig(fig, "fig_open_paid_by_cohort", width="double") fig ``` ::: {#c210 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: #### B.8.3 Paying population by age **Method.** Paying population by age band. **Data.** ICMS extract (1.3), December 2025 snapshot [lab: era março de 2026], legal entities only; unit of observation: the CDA. **How to read.** One row per age band with numbers of CDAs, of paying CDAs and the share paying. **Interpretation.** A declining share with age indicates that older debts are less likely to have ever been paid. *Output:* Table `tab_payers_age`. ::: {#cell-c212 .cell execution_count=19} ``` {.python .cell-code} payers_age = cda.with_columns(((pl.date(SNAP_YEAR, SNAP_MONTH, 1) - pl.col("DATA_INSCRICAO")).dt.total_days() / 365.25).alias("age")) \ .with_columns(band()).group_by("age_band").agg(pl.len().alias("n_cda"), pl.col("ever_paid").sum().alias("n_paid")) \ .with_columns((100 * pl.col("n_paid") / pl.col("n_cda")).alias("pct_paid"), pl.col("age_band").cast(pl.Utf8)).sort("age_band") save_tab(payers_age, "tab_payers_age", fmt="{:,.2f}") payers_age ``` ::: {#c212 .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=19} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: #### B.8.4 Time to first payment **Method.** Delay between enrolment and first payment among paying CDAs. **Data.** ICMS extract (1.3), CDAs enrolled from 2016 onward with at least one payment. **How to read.** Vertical bars by whole years from enrolment to first payment, the last grouping ten years or more; the vertical axis gives the share of paying CDAs, printed above each bar. **Interpretation.** Mass in the first bar means that, among CDAs that are paid at all, payment usually starts soon after enrolment. *Output:* Figure `fig_delay_first_gare`. ::: {#cell-c214 .cell execution_count=20} ``` {.python .cell-code} delay = cda.filter(pl.col("ever_paid") & (pl.col("DATA_INSCRICAO") >= pl.date(YEARS[0], 1, 1))) \ .with_columns(pl.col("years_to_first_payment").floor().cast(pl.Int32).clip(0, 10).alias("delay")).group_by("delay").len().sort("delay") delay = delay.with_columns((100 * pl.col("len") / pl.col("len").sum()).alias("pct")) fig = go.Figure(go.Bar(x=delay["delay"], y=delay["pct"], marker_color=CEMEPI["deep_teal"], text=[f"{v:.0f}%" for v in delay["pct"]], textposition="outside")) fig.update_layout(xaxis_title="Years from enrolment to first payment (10 = 10 or more)", yaxis_title="Share of paying CDAs (%)") save_fig(fig, "fig_delay_first_gare") fig ``` ::: {#c214 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: #### B.8.5 Time to settlement **Method.** Time to settlement, approximated by the exit of a CDA from the snapshots after at least one payment, because settlement is not recorded. **Data.** ICMS extract (1.3), CDAs with a payment that left the snapshots before December 2025 [lab: era março de 2026]. **How to read.** Histogram; the horizontal axis gives years from enrolment to exit, the vertical axis numbers of CDAs. **Interpretation.** Exits can also result from cancellation, so the proxy is an upper bound on settlement times. *Output:* Figure `fig_settlement_proxy`. :::{.callout-note} ## B.8.5 com valor no eixo Y Além do histograma do paper (número de CDAs), a célula abaixo mostra o valor inscrito em R$ bilhões por ano até a saída. A versão com valor pago está em [Concentração e liquidação](../eda/2026-10-23_concentracao_e_liquidacao.qmd). ::: ::: {#c216 .cell execution_count=21} ``` {.python .cell-code} last_snap = SNAP_YEAR * 100 + SNAP_MONTH settled = cda.filter((pl.col("last_snapshot") < last_snap) & pl.col("ever_paid")).with_columns( ((pl.date(pl.col("last_snapshot") // 100, pl.col("last_snapshot") % 100, 1) - pl.col("DATA_INSCRICAO")).dt.total_days() / 365.25).alias("years_to_exit")) fig = go.Figure(go.Histogram(x=settled["years_to_exit"].clip(0, 20), nbinsx=40, marker_color=CEMEPI["deep_teal"])) fig.update_layout(xaxis_title="Years from enrolment to exit after payment (settlement proxy)", yaxis_title="CDAs") save_fig(fig, "fig_settlement_proxy") # lab: o mesmo recorte com o valor no eixo Y (R$ bilhões), pedido na reunião de 23/10/2026 _vcol = "max_value" if "max_value" in settled.columns else None _set = settled.with_columns(pl.col("years_to_exit").clip(0, 20).floor().alias("years_bin")) _agg = [pl.len().alias("cdas")] + ([(pl.col(_vcol).sum() / 1e9).alias("value_bn")] if _vcol else []) _val = _set.group_by("years_bin").agg(*_agg).sort("years_bin") fig.show() fig_val = make_subplots(rows=2, cols=1, shared_xaxes=True, row_heights=[0.65, 0.35], vertical_spacing=0.06) if _vcol: fig_val.add_trace(go.Bar(x=_val["years_bin"], y=_val["value_bn"], marker_color=CEMEPI["deep_teal"], name="Enrolled value (max., R$ bn)"), 1, 1) fig_val.add_trace(go.Bar(x=_val["years_bin"], y=_val["cdas"], marker_color=CEMEPI["sand"], name="CDAs"), 2, 1) fig_val.update_yaxes(title_text="R$ billion", row=1, col=1) fig_val.update_yaxes(title_text="CDAs", row=2, col=1) fig_val.update_xaxes(title_text="Years from enrolment to exit after payment", row=2, col=1) fig_val.update_layout(showlegend=True, legend=dict(orientation="h", y=1.08)) fig_val ``` ::: {#c216-1 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: #### B.8.6 Age windows of payments **Method.** Distribution of payments by age of the CDA at the time of payment, and the payment hazard per exposed CDA-year. **Data.** GARE payments linked to ICMS CDAs, 2016–2025 [lab: era 2016–2026]; exposure from the panel. **How to read.** Grouped bars by age band (youngest to oldest); the vertical axis gives the share of payment records and of the amount paid, identified in the legend. The table adds the hazard. **Interpretation.** A band whose value bar exceeds its count bar receives fewer but larger payments. *Output:* Figure `fig_gare_window_life`; Table `tab_gare_window`. ::: {#cell-c218 .cell execution_count=22} ``` {.python .cell-code} def gare_windows() -> pl.DataFrame: g = scan_gare().join(attributes.select("ID_DEBITO", "DATA_INSCRICAO"), on="ID_DEBITO").with_columns( ((pl.col("DATA_ARRECADACAO_GARE") - pl.col("DATA_INSCRICAO")).dt.total_days() / 365.25).alias("age")) g = g.with_columns(band()) pay = collect(g.group_by("age_band").agg(pl.len().alias("payments"), pl.col("ID_DEBITO").n_unique().alias("cda_paying"), pl.col("VALOR_RECEITA").sum().alias("value"))) expo = collect(panel.with_columns(band()).group_by("age_band").agg(pl.len().alias("cda_years"))) return pay.join(expo, on="age_band").with_columns( (100 * pl.col("payments") / pl.col("payments").sum()).alias("pct_payments"), (100 * pl.col("value") / pl.col("value").sum()).alias("pct_value"), (pl.col("cda_paying") / pl.col("cda_years")).alias("hazard"), pl.col("age_band").cast(pl.Utf8)) windows = collect(cached("B.8.6", gare_windows, params=EXTRACT_PARAMS)).sort("age_band") fig = go.Figure([go.Bar(x=windows["age_band"], y=windows[c], name=n, marker_color=color(i)) for i, (c, n) in enumerate((("pct_payments", "Payments"), ("pct_value", "Value paid")))]) fig.update_layout(barmode="group", xaxis_title="Age of CDA at payment (years)", yaxis_title="Share (%)", showlegend=True, legend=dict(orientation="h", y=1.1)) save_fig(fig, "fig_gare_window_life") save_tab(windows, "tab_gare_window", fmt="{:,.4f}") fig ``` ::: {#c218 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: #### B.8.7 Cohort by horizon **Method.** Cumulative share of CDAs with a payment by cohort and horizon. **Data.** ICMS extract (1.3), cohorts 2016–2025 [lab: era 2016–2026]. **How to read.** Heat map: rows are enrolment cohorts, columns years since enrolment; colour and printed values give the percentage with any payment, as shown by the colour bar. **Interpretation.** Read along a row for the speed of payment of a cohort and down a column to compare cohorts at the same horizon; the triangle arises because later cohorts are observed for fewer years. *Output:* Figure `fig_cohort_horizon`. ::: {#cell-c220 .cell execution_count=23} ``` {.python .cell-code} horizon = (cda.filter(pl.col("DATA_INSCRICAO").dt.year() >= YEARS[0]) .with_columns(pl.col("DATA_INSCRICAO").dt.year().alias("cohort"), (pl.col("first_payment").dt.year() - pl.col("DATA_INSCRICAO").dt.year()).alias("h"))) size = horizon.group_by("cohort").len() cells = [] for h in range(0, SNAP_YEAR - YEARS[0] + 1): c = horizon.group_by("cohort").agg((pl.col("h") <= h).sum().alias("n")).with_columns(pl.lit(h).alias("h")) cells.append(c) grid = pl.concat(cells).join(size, on="cohort").with_columns( pl.when(pl.col("cohort") + pl.col("h") <= SNAP_YEAR).then(100 * pl.col("n") / pl.col("len")).alias("pct")) mat = grid.pivot(on="h", index="cohort", values="pct").sort("cohort").with_columns(pl.col("cohort").cast(pl.Utf8)) fig = heatmap(mat, "cohort", diverging=False, zmin=0, fmt="{:.0f}", colorbar_title="% with payment") fig.update_layout(xaxis_title="Years since enrolment", yaxis_title="Enrolment cohort") save_fig(fig, "fig_cohort_horizon", width="double") fig ``` ::: {#c220 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: #### B.8.8 Annual collection **Method.** Annual GARE collection on ICMS CDAs. **Data.** GARE payments linked to ICMS CDAs, 2016–2025 [lab: era 2016–2026]. **How to read.** Vertical bars by year; the vertical axis gives R$ billion, printed above each bar. **Interpretation.** The final year covers January to March only and is not comparable with full years. *Output:* Figure `fig_gare_annual`. ::: {#cell-c222 .cell execution_count=24} ``` {.python .cell-code} gare_annual = collect(scan_gare().group_by(pl.col("DATA_ARRECADACAO_GARE").dt.year().alias("year")) .agg((pl.col("VALOR_RECEITA").sum() / 1e9).alias("collected_bn")).sort("year")) fig = go.Figure(go.Bar(x=gare_annual["year"], y=gare_annual["collected_bn"], marker_color=CEMEPI["deep_teal"], text=[f"{v:.2f}" for v in gare_annual["collected_bn"]], textposition="outside")) fig.update_layout(yaxis_title="GARE collection on ICMS CDAs (R$ bn)") save_fig(fig, "fig_gare_annual") fig ``` ::: {#c222 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### B.9 Judicial filing *No new terms are introduced in this section; terms used here are defined in the Glossary.* #### B.9.1 Filing status of the portfolio **Method.** Composition of the stock by judicial filing status. The Portuguese categories are translated; records whose status code does not match a documented category are grouped as *unrecognised code*. **Data.** Year-end snapshots of the ICMS extract, 2016–2025 [lab: era 2016–2026]; unit of observation: the status-year. **How to read.** The horizontal axis gives the year; the vertical axis the share of year-end stock in percent; one line per status, identified in the legend. **Interpretation.** A stable dominant share for *filed* indicates that most of the stock is under judicial collection. *Output:* Figure `fig_filing_status`; Table `tab_filing_status`. ::: {#cell-c225 .cell execution_count=25} ``` {.python .cell-code} filing_year = collect(year_end.with_columns(filing_label()).group_by("year", "STATUS_AJUIZAMENTO_DEBITO").agg( pl.len().alias("n_cda"), (pl.col("stock").sum() / 1e9).alias("stock_bn"))).with_columns( (100 * pl.col("stock_bn") / pl.col("stock_bn").sum().over("year")).alias("pct_stock")).sort("year") fig = lines(filing_year, "year", "pct_stock", "STATUS_AJUIZAMENTO_DEBITO", y_title="Share of year-end stock (%)", order=list(FILING_LABELS.values()) + ["Unrecognised code"]) save_fig(fig, "fig_filing_status", width="double") save_tab(filing_year.filter(pl.col("year") == SNAP_YEAR), "tab_filing_status", fmt="{:,.2f}") fig ``` ::: {#c225 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: #### B.9.2 Filing by age and value **Method.** Filing by age band and by value decile. **Data.** ICMS extract (1.3), December 2025 snapshot [lab: era março de 2026], legal entities only; unit of observation: the CDA. **How to read.** Left: bars of the share of CDAs filed by age band. Right: bars of the share of CDAs filed by value decile (1 = smallest tenth, 10 = largest) and a line for the share of stock filed within each decile; the legend identifies the series. **Interpretation.** Rising bars indicate that older and larger debts are more likely to be filed. *Output:* Figure `fig_filing_age_value`. ::: {#cell-c227 .cell execution_count=26} ``` {.python .cell-code} fv = raw_values.with_columns(band(), (pl.col("value").rank() * 10 / pl.len()).ceil().cast(pl.Int32).alias("decile"), (pl.col("STATUS_AJUIZAMENTO_DEBITO") == "Ajuizado").alias("filed")) by_age = fv.group_by("age_band").agg((100 * pl.col("filed").mean()).alias("pct")).with_columns(pl.col("age_band").cast(pl.Utf8)).sort("age_band") by_dec = fv.group_by("decile").agg((100 * pl.col("filed").mean()).alias("pct"), (100 * pl.col("value").filter(pl.col("filed")).sum() / pl.col("value").sum()).alias("pct_value")).sort("decile") fig = make_subplots(rows=1, cols=2, horizontal_spacing=0.12) fig.add_trace(go.Bar(x=by_age["age_band"], y=by_age["pct"], marker_color=CEMEPI["deep_teal"], name="Share of CDAs filed", legendgroup="n"), 1, 1) fig.add_trace(go.Bar(x=by_dec["decile"], y=by_dec["pct"], marker_color=CEMEPI["deep_teal"], name="Share of CDAs filed", legendgroup="n", showlegend=False), 1, 2) fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=by_dec["decile"], y=by_dec["pct_value"], mode="lines+markers", line_color=CEMEPI["sand"], name="Share of stock filed"), 1, 2) fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Filed in court (%)", row=1, col=2) fig.update_xaxes(tickmode="array", tickvals=list(range(1, 11)), row=1, col=2) fig.update_layout(showlegend=True, legend=dict(orientation="h", y=-0.3)) fig.update_xaxes(title_text="Age band (years)", row=1, col=1) fig.update_xaxes(title_text="Value decile", row=1, col=2) fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Filed in court (%)", row=1, col=1) save_fig(fig, "fig_filing_age_value", width="double") fig ``` ::: {#c227 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: #### B.9.3 Time to filing **Method.** Time from enrolment to filing for CDAs whose status changes to filed during the observation window. **Data.** ICMS extract (1.3), 2016–2025 [lab: era 2016–2026]. **How to read.** Histogram; the horizontal axis gives years from enrolment to the first snapshot as filed (capped at 15), the vertical axis numbers of CDAs. **Interpretation.** CDAs already filed at their first observation are excluded, so the distribution describes recent filing practice. *Output:* Figure `fig_time_to_filing`. ::: {#cell-c229 .cell execution_count=27} ``` {.python .cell-code} filed_later = cda.filter(pl.col("first_filed_snapshot").is_not_null() & (pl.col("first_filed_snapshot") > pl.col("first_snapshot"))) \ .with_columns(((pl.date(pl.col("first_filed_snapshot") // 100, pl.col("first_filed_snapshot") % 100, 1) - pl.col("DATA_INSCRICAO")) .dt.total_days() / 365.25).alias("years_to_filing")) fig = go.Figure(go.Histogram(x=filed_later["years_to_filing"].clip(0, 15), nbinsx=45, marker_color=CEMEPI["deep_teal"])) fig.update_layout(xaxis_title="Years from enrolment to judicial filing", yaxis_title="CDAs") save_fig(fig, "fig_time_to_filing") fig ``` ::: {#c229 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: #### B.9.4 Payments and recovery by filing status **Method.** Amount paid by age band and filing status. **Data.** ICMS CDA × year panel (1.4), legal entities only, 2016–2025 [lab: era 2016–2026]; unit of observation: the CDA-year. **How to read.** Stacked vertical bars by age band (youngest to oldest); the vertical axis gives the amount paid 2016–2025 [lab: era 2016–2026] in R$ billion; segments correspond to filing statuses, identified in the legend. **Interpretation.** If payments on older debts come mainly from filed CDAs, this is consistent with judicial collection supporting recovery at advanced ages; the table adds payment shares and rates. *Output:* Figure `fig_recovery_by_filing`; Table `tab_recovery_by_filing`. ::: {#cell-c231 .cell execution_count=28} ``` {.python .cell-code} rec_filing = collect(panel.with_columns(band(), filing_label()).group_by("STATUS_AJUIZAMENTO_DEBITO", "age_band").agg( pl.len().alias("cda_years"), (100 * pl.col("paid_flag").mean()).alias("pct_paying"), (100 * pl.col("paid").sum() / pl.col("stock").sum()).alias("rate_pct"), (pl.col("paid").sum() / 1e9).alias("paid_bn")) .with_columns(pl.col("age_band").cast(pl.Utf8)).sort("STATUS_AJUIZAMENTO_DEBITO", "age_band")) fig = go.Figure([go.Bar(x=d["age_band"], y=d["paid_bn"], name=k[0], marker_color=color(i)) for i, (k, d) in enumerate(rec_filing.group_by("STATUS_AJUIZAMENTO_DEBITO", maintain_order=True))]) fig.update_layout(barmode="stack", xaxis_title="Age band (years)", yaxis_title="Amount paid 2016-2025 (R$ bn)", showlegend=True, legend=dict(orientation="h", y=1.12)) save_fig(fig, "fig_recovery_by_filing", width="double") save_tab(rec_filing, "tab_recovery_by_filing", fmt="{:,.3f}") fig ``` ::: {#c231 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: #### B.9.5 Payments around the filing date **Method.** Event-time profile of payments around filing: CDAs are aligned on the month in which their status changes to filed (month 0). **Data.** ICMS extract (1.3) and GARE payments, CDAs filed during the window. **How to read.** The horizontal axis gives months relative to filing (−12 to 12); the vertical axis the percentage of CDAs with a payment in that month; the dotted line marks month 0. **Interpretation.** A rise after month 0 is consistent with filing prompting payment, but alignment alone does not establish causation, since filing may target debts likely to pay. *Output:* Figure `fig_payment_around_filing`. ::: {#cell-c233 .cell execution_count=29} ``` {.python .cell-code} ev = filed_later.select("ID_DEBITO", (pl.col("first_filed_snapshot") // 100 * 12 + pl.col("first_filed_snapshot") % 100).alias("filed_m")) pay_m = collect(scan_gare().join(ev.lazy(), on="ID_DEBITO").with_columns( (pl.col("DATA_ARRECADACAO_GARE").dt.year() * 12 + pl.col("DATA_ARRECADACAO_GARE").dt.month() - pl.col("filed_m")).alias("k")) .filter(pl.col("k").is_between(-12, 12)).group_by("k").agg(pl.col("ID_DEBITO").n_unique().alias("paying"))) pay_m = pay_m.with_columns((100 * pl.col("paying") / ev.height).alias("hazard")).sort("k") fig = go.Figure(go.Scatter(x=pay_m["k"], y=pay_m["hazard"], mode="lines+markers", line_color=CEMEPI["deep_teal"])) fig.add_vline(x=0, line_dash="dot", line_color=CEMEPI["sand"]) fig.update_layout(xaxis_title="Months relative to judicial filing", yaxis_title="CDAs with a payment (%)") save_fig(fig, "fig_payment_around_filing") fig ``` ::: {#c233 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: #### B.9.6 Filing by origin and debtor size **Method.** Filing by origin and by concentration stratum. **Data.** ICMS extract (1.3), December 2025 snapshot [lab: era março de 2026], legal entities only; unit of observation: the CDA. **How to read.** One row per origin and stratum (top 0.1%, top 1%, remainder), with shares of CDAs and stock filed. **Interpretation.** Differences indicate whether filing priorities depend on origin or debt size. *Output:* Table `tab_filing_origin_size`. ::: {#cell-c235 .cell execution_count=30} ``` {.python .cell-code} filing_origin_size = strata.group_by("ICMS_ORIGIN", "stratum").agg( pl.len().alias("n_cda"), (100 * (pl.col("STATUS_AJUIZAMENTO_DEBITO") == "Ajuizado").mean()).alias("pct_filed"), (100 * pl.col("value").filter(pl.col("STATUS_AJUIZAMENTO_DEBITO") == "Ajuizado").sum() / pl.col("value").sum()).alias("pct_stock_filed") ).sort("ICMS_ORIGIN", "stratum") save_tab(filing_origin_size, "tab_filing_origin_size", fmt="{:,.2f}") filing_origin_size ``` ::: {#c235 .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=30} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ### B.10 Seasonality *Terms introduced in this section:* Seasonality, STL. Definitions are given in the Glossary. #### B.10.1 Seasonality of enrolments **Method.** Seasonality of enrolments: mean number of new CDAs by calendar month across years, with a 95% interval (1.96 standard errors across years). **Data.** Monthly ICMS series (1.5), January 2016 to December 2025 [lab: era até março de 2026]; unit of observation: the month. Full years only. **How to read.** Vertical bars by calendar month; the vertical axis gives new CDAs in thousands; error bars give the interval; the dotted line marks the overall monthly mean. **Interpretation.** Months whose interval lies entirely above or below the line show a systematic seasonal deviation. *Output:* Figure `fig_seasonality_enrolment`. ::: {#cell-c238 .cell execution_count=31} ``` {.python .cell-code} season = monthly_all.with_columns(pl.col("month").dt.month().alias("m"), pl.col("month").dt.year().alias("y")) \ .filter(pl.col("y") <= LAB_LAST_YEAR).group_by("m").agg(pl.col("n_new").mean().alias("mean"), pl.col("n_new").std().alias("sd"), pl.len().alias("n")).sort("m") season = season.with_columns((1.96 * pl.col("sd") / pl.col("n").sqrt()).alias("ci")) fig = go.Figure(go.Bar(x=season["m"], y=season["mean"] / 1e3, marker_color=CEMEPI["deep_teal"], error_y=dict(type="data", array=(season["ci"] / 1e3).to_list(), color=CEMEPI["sand"]))) fig.add_hline(y=season["mean"].mean() / 1e3, line_dash="dot", line_color=CEMEPI["grey"]) fig.update_layout(xaxis=dict(title="Calendar month", tickmode="array", tickvals=list(range(1, 13))), yaxis_title="New ICMS CDAs (thousand, mean)") save_fig(fig, "fig_seasonality_enrolment") fig ``` ::: {#c238 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: #### B.10.2 Monthly collection **Method.** Monthly collection with peaks highlighted. **Data.** Monthly ICMS series (1.5), January 2016 to December 2025 [lab: era até março de 2026]; unit of observation: the month. **How to read.** The horizontal axis gives the month; the vertical axis collection in R$ billion; months above the 95th percentile are labelled with their date; cream bands mark programme windows. **Interpretation.** Peaks inside the bands are associated with programmes; isolated peaks outside them point to other events. *Output:* Figure `fig_monthly_collection`. ::: {#cell-c240 .cell execution_count=32} ``` {.python .cell-code} coll = monthly_all.select("month", "collection").with_columns(bn(pl.col("collection")).alias("bn")) p95 = coll["bn"].quantile(0.95) fig = go.Figure(go.Scatter(x=coll["month"], y=coll["bn"], mode="lines", line_color=CEMEPI["deep_teal"])) for j, r in enumerate(coll.filter(pl.col("bn") > p95).iter_rows(named=True)): fig.add_annotation(x=r["month"], y=r["bn"], text=r["month"].strftime("%b %Y"), showarrow=False, yshift=8, font_size=9, xanchor="right" if j % 2 == 0 else "left") shade_programmes(fig) fig.update_layout(yaxis_title="Monthly collection (R$ bn)") save_fig(fig, "fig_monthly_collection", width="double") fig ``` ::: {#c240 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: #### B.10.3 Seasonal decomposition **Method.** Robust STL decomposition (Seasonal-Trend decomposition using Loess; Cleveland et al., 1990) of log monthly collection into trend, a twelve-month seasonal component that may evolve slowly, and a remainder. The robust version down-weights outliers so that programme peaks do not distort trend and seasonality. **Data.** Monthly ICMS series (1.5), January 2016 to December 2025 [lab: era até março de 2026]; unit of observation: the month. Full years only. **How to read.** Decomposition figure: panels from top to bottom give the observed series, trend, seasonal component and remainder. Sub-series figure: one panel per calendar month, with that month's values across years and a horizontal line at their mean; the legend identifies the two elements. **Interpretation.** Differences between the monthly means describe the seasonal pattern; trends within panels show whether it changes over time; large spikes in the remainder are irregular events. *Output:* Figures `fig_stl`, `fig_seasonal_subseries`. ::: {#c242 .cell execution_count=33} ``` {.python .cell-code} from statsmodels.tsa.seasonal import STL y = monthly_all.filter(pl.col("month") <= pl.date(LAB_LAST_YEAR, 12, 1)) # lab: 2025 completo entra.select("month", "collection") stl = STL(np.log(y["collection"].to_numpy()), period=12, robust=True).fit() fig = make_subplots(rows=4, cols=1, shared_xaxes=True, vertical_spacing=0.03) for r, (series, name) in enumerate(((stl.observed, "log collection"), (stl.trend, "trend"), (stl.seasonal, "seasonal"), (stl.resid, "remainder")), start=1): fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=y["month"], y=series, mode="lines", line_color=color(r - 1)), r, 1) fig.update_yaxes(title_text=name, row=r, col=1) save_fig(fig, "fig_stl", width="double", ratio=0.9) fig.show() sub = y.with_columns(pl.col("month").dt.month().alias("m"), pl.col("month").dt.year().alias("yr"), pl.col("collection").log().alias("lc")) fig = make_subplots(rows=1, cols=12, shared_yaxes=True, horizontal_spacing=0.005) for m in range(1, 13): d = sub.filter(pl.col("m") == m).sort("yr") fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=d["yr"], y=d["lc"], mode="lines", line_color=CEMEPI["deep_teal"], name="Collection in that month, by year", legendgroup="y", showlegend=m == 1), 1, m) fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=[d["yr"].min(), d["yr"].max()], y=[d["lc"].mean()] * 2, mode="lines", line_color=CEMEPI["sand"], name="Mean across years", legendgroup="m", showlegend=m == 1), 1, m) fig.update_xaxes(showticklabels=False, title_text=str(m), row=1, col=m) fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Monthly collection (log R$)", row=1, col=1) fig.update_layout(showlegend=True, legend=dict(orientation="h", y=-0.3), annotations=[*fig.layout.annotations, dict(text="Calendar month", x=0.5, y=-0.12, xref="paper", yref="paper", showarrow=False)]) save_fig(fig, "fig_seasonal_subseries", width="double") fig ``` ::: {#c242-1 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: #### B.10.4 Seasonality by origin **Method.** Seasonal profile of enrolments by origin, normalised by each origin's monthly mean. **Data.** Monthly ICMS series (1.5), January 2016 to December 2025 [lab: era até março de 2026]; unit of observation: the month. Declared and assessed debts. **How to read.** The horizontal axis gives the calendar month; the vertical axis enrolments relative to the origin's mean (1 = average month); one line per origin, identified in the legend. **Interpretation.** Different profiles would be consistent with assessed debts following the calendar of administrative appeals rather than that of declarations. *Output:* Figure `fig_seasonality_by_type`. ::: {#cell-c244 .cell execution_count=34} ``` {.python .cell-code} season_origin = monthly.filter(pl.col("ICMS_ORIGIN").is_in(["declared", "assessed"])).with_columns( pl.col("month").dt.month().alias("m")).group_by("ICMS_ORIGIN", "m").agg(pl.col("n_new").mean()).with_columns( (pl.col("n_new") / pl.col("n_new").mean().over("ICMS_ORIGIN")).alias("index")) fig = lines(season_origin, "m", "index", "ICMS_ORIGIN", y_title="Enrolments relative to origin mean", x_title="Calendar month") fig.update_xaxes(tickmode="array", tickvals=list(range(1, 13))) save_fig(fig, "fig_seasonality_by_type") fig ``` ::: {#c244 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### B.11 Settlement programmes *No new terms are introduced in this section; terms used here are defined in the Glossary.* #### B.11.1 Programme calendar **Method.** Calendar of settlement programmes. **Data.** Programme regulations. **How to read.** One row per programme, with dates and main terms. **Interpretation.** The windows defined here are used throughout the notebook. *Output:* Table `tab_editais`. ::: {#cell-c247 .cell execution_count=35} ``` {.python .cell-code} editais = pl.DataFrame([ ("PEP 2019", "Programa Especial de Parcelamento do ICMS", "2019", "Reduced fines and interest; instalments for ICMS debts"), ("Acordo Paulista 2024", "Transação tributária (Lei 17.843/2023)", "2024", "Negotiated settlements with discounts by recoverability class"), ], schema=["programme", "instrument", "year", "main_terms"], orient="row").with_columns( pl.Series("window_start", [p[1] for p in PROGRAMMES]), pl.Series("window_end", [p[2] for p in PROGRAMMES])) save_tab(editais, "tab_editais") editais ``` ::: {#c247 .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=35} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: #### B.11.2 Programme windows **Method.** Collection around programme start, indexed to the pre-programme mean. **Data.** Monthly ICMS series (1.5), January 2016 to December 2025 [lab: era até março de 2026]; unit of observation: the month. **How to read.** The horizontal axis gives months relative to the start (0 = first month, dotted line); the vertical axis collection indexed so that the pre-programme mean equals 100; one line per programme, identified in the legend. **Interpretation.** Indexing removes differences in level, so the curves compare the relative size and timing of each programme's effect. *Output:* Figure `fig_edital_windows`. ::: {#cell-c249 .cell execution_count=36} ``` {.python .cell-code} rows = [] for name, start, _ in PROGRAMMES: s = np.datetime64(start, "M") d = monthly_all.with_columns(((pl.col("month").dt.year() - int(start[:4])) * 12 + pl.col("month").dt.month() - int(start[5:7])).alias("k")) \ .filter(pl.col("k").is_between(-12, 12)) base = d.filter(pl.col("k") < 0).select(pl.col("collection").mean(), pl.col("n_payers").mean()) rows.append(d.with_columns((100 * pl.col("collection") / base["collection"][0]).alias("collection_idx"), (100 * pl.col("n_payers") / base["n_payers"][0]).alias("payers_idx"), pl.lit(name).alias("programme"))) win = pl.concat(rows) fig = lines(win, "k", "collection_idx", "programme", y_title="Collection (pre-programme mean = 100)", x_title="Months relative to programme start") fig.add_vline(x=0, line_dash="dot", line_color=CEMEPI["grey"]) save_fig(fig, "fig_edital_windows", width="double") fig ``` ::: {#c249 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: #### B.11.3 Arrears before programmes **Method.** New enrolments before each programme, indexed to months −24 to −13. **Data.** Monthly ICMS series (1.5), January 2016 to December 2025 [lab: era até março de 2026]; unit of observation: the month. **How to read.** The horizontal axis gives months before the start; the vertical axis new enrolments indexed so that the mean of months −24 to −13 equals 100; one line per programme, identified in the legend. **Interpretation.** A rise in the final months would be consistent with arrears building up in anticipation of favourable terms; isolated spikes may reflect batch enrolments. *Output:* Figure `fig_pre_programme`. ::: {#cell-c251 .cell execution_count=37} ``` {.python .cell-code} pre = [] for name, start, _ in PROGRAMMES: d = monthly_all.with_columns(((pl.col("month").dt.year() - int(start[:4])) * 12 + pl.col("month").dt.month() - int(start[5:7])).alias("k")) \ .filter(pl.col("k").is_between(-24, 0)) base = d.filter(pl.col("k") <= -13)["n_new"].mean() pre.append(d.with_columns((100 * pl.col("n_new") / base).alias("new_idx"), pl.lit(name).alias("programme"))) fig = lines(pl.concat(pre), "k", "new_idx", "programme", y_title="New enrolments (months -24 to -13 = 100)", x_title="Months before programme start") save_fig(fig, "fig_pre_programme", width="double") fig ``` ::: {#c251 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: #### B.11.4 The 2024 peak **Method.** Decomposition of the change in collection from 2023 to 2024 by origin, age band and debtor size. **Data.** ICMS CDA × year panel (1.4), legal entities only, 2016–2025 [lab: era 2016–2026]; unit of observation: the CDA-year. Years 2023 and 2024. **How to read.** One row per category within each dimension, with the increase in R$ billion and its share of the total increase within the dimension. **Interpretation.** Categories with large shares drive the 2024 peak; negative shares indicate categories whose collection fell. *Output:* Table `tab_2024_peak`. ::: {#cell-c253 .cell execution_count=38} ``` {.python .cell-code} peak = collect(panel.filter(pl.col("year").is_in([2023, 2024])).with_columns(band()).with_columns(pl.col("age_band").cast(pl.Utf8)) .join(pl.DataFrame({"ID_DEBITO": list(top_ids)}).lazy().with_columns(pl.lit("top 1%").alias("size")), on="ID_DEBITO", how="left") .with_columns(pl.col("size").fill_null("remainder"))) rows = [] for dim in ("ICMS_ORIGIN", "age_band", "size"): g = peak.group_by(dim, "year").agg(pl.col("paid").sum()).pivot(on="year", index=dim, values="paid").rename({dim: "category"}) rows.append(g.select(pl.col("category").cast(pl.Utf8), pl.col("2023"), pl.col("2024")).with_columns(pl.lit(dim).alias("dimension"))) peak_tab = pl.concat(rows).with_columns(((pl.col("2024") - pl.col("2023")) / 1e9).alias("increase_bn")) peak_tab = peak_tab.with_columns((100 * pl.col("increase_bn") / pl.col("increase_bn").sum().over("dimension")).alias("pct_of_increase")) save_tab(peak_tab.select("dimension", "category", "increase_bn", "pct_of_increase"), "tab_2024_peak", fmt="{:,.3f}") peak_tab ``` ::: {#c253 .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=38} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: #### B.11.5 Peaks of the observed series **Method.** Monthly collection as a scatter with peaks highlighted. **Data.** Monthly ICMS series (1.5), January 2016 to December 2025 [lab: era até março de 2026]; unit of observation: the month. **How to read.** Each point is one month; the vertical axis gives collection in R$ billion; highlighted points above the 95th percentile (dotted line) are labelled with their date; cream bands mark programme windows. **Interpretation.** The proportion of highlighted points inside the bands indicates how much of the extreme collection is programme-driven. *Output:* Figure `fig_peaks_scatter`. ::: {#cell-c255 .cell execution_count=39} ``` {.python .cell-code} peaks = coll.with_columns((pl.col("bn") > p95).alias("peak")) fig = go.Figure([go.Scatter(x=peaks.filter(~pl.col("peak"))["month"], y=peaks.filter(~pl.col("peak"))["bn"], mode="markers", marker=dict(size=5, color=CEMEPI["grey"])), go.Scatter(x=peaks.filter(pl.col("peak"))["month"], y=peaks.filter(pl.col("peak"))["bn"], mode="markers+text", marker=dict(size=8, color=CEMEPI["sand"]), text=[m.strftime("%b %Y") for m in peaks.filter(pl.col("peak"))["month"]], textposition="top center", textfont_size=9)]) fig.add_hline(y=p95, line_dash="dot", line_color=CEMEPI["deep_teal"], annotation_text="95th percentile") shade_programmes(fig) fig.update_layout(yaxis_title="Monthly collection (R$ bn)") save_fig(fig, "fig_peaks_scatter", width="double") fig ``` ::: {#c255 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
